9. Performance Strategy
-----------------------

LCP at p75 mobile is the binding constraint and the de-facto cap on third-party script weight.

| Metric | Target |
| --- | --- |
| LCP (mobile p75) | ≤ 2 s |
| Lighthouse Performance | ≥ 0.80 |
| Lighthouse Accessibility | ≥ 0.90 |
| Lighthouse Best Practices | ≥ 0.90 |

### 9.1 Third-party defer rule

Anything loaded via Didomi callback (GTM — which loads Meta, GA4, and other GTM-housed tags via Tell No Lies; Narvar EDD widget; Inside Chat) is deferred, async-loaded, or injected post-hydration so it does not block LCP. **Measmerize** (Find My Size / size guide — PDP only) likewise defers behind LCP — the script injects after the product hero image has loaded. **reCAPTCHA** likewise loads only on register/login form interaction, so it never sits on the critical path of any other page (consent treatment per §11.1). **Exception (AAB-004):** Optimizely Web is a PWA-direct head tag (not a GTM tag) and deliberately loads in the page head **before render** to prevent A/B flicker, scoped to the US storefront where Optimizely runs. **Crazy Egg (AAB-005)** loads async and post-Didomi-consent. Both load strictly post-Didomi-consent; keep both snippets minimal.

### 9.2 Other levers

* **Images:** all storefront imagery — product and editorial — is stored in and served from **Contentful** (`images.ctfassets.net`) via the Contentful Images API; SFCC holds no image assets (DMU-010 migration de-scoped; product images CRM-075; all media via the CMS library HPC-003). The PWA generates `srcset` / `sizes` and sets size, quality, and format per breakpoint on the asset URL — **AVIF primary with WebP / JPEG fallbacks**. Lazy-load all non-LCP images; priority-load the primary hero image (PRD-064). Never render full-resolution images at thumbnail size.
* **Video:** sourced by platform, not self-hosted, so codec / adaptive-streaming selection belongs to the upstream player rather than to this layer:

  + **Product videos → Vimeo**, referenced by embed URL stored in product data or the CMS (PRD-067). Load behind a lightweight facade (poster image + click/scroll-to-load) so the Vimeo player JS never lands on the LCP critical path.
  + **Content-managed page videos → Contentful** by default, served from the Contentful asset CDN and referenced within the CMS content entry alongside the page content. Editorial pages may also embed a Vimeo video by URL where preferred (HPC-004) — the product/editorial split above is the expected pattern, not a hard restriction.
  + Across both: `preload="metadata"` by default; autoplay reserved for muted, short-loop hero clips only.
* Dynamic imports for heavy non-initial components.
* Parallel data fetches; no client-side waterfalls. Fetch only required fields.

### 9.3 Where performance is measured

The CI Lighthouse gate (§14.3) catches regressions but runs against the Dev-tier MRT deployment — slower than production hardware, further from the edge, and not representative of the LCP a real shopper experiences. The signed-off LCP and Lighthouse targets in this section are therefore validated against **Stage**, which mirrors production infrastructure (same MRT bundle size class, same CDN/edge configuration, same SFCC realm tier). Treat CI numbers as regression indicators; treat Stage numbers as the contractual ones.

> **SSR connection pool tuning:** the initial per-pool connection caps defined in §12.1 are derived from expected concurrency, not observed traffic. The first Stage performance run should include per-pool queue-depth and connection-wait metrics (undici emits these as diagnostic channel events). Use those numbers to validate or revise the caps.

12. Graceful Degradation
------------------------

Each external system fails independently — one outage does not break a page.

| System | Failure mode |
| --- | --- |
| Contentful | Render page without editorial content; never block commerce data on CMS |
| Global-e | Surface explicit error; do not silently fall back to SFCC for international checkout |
| Didomi | Fail closed — no consent, no third-party scripts |
| Omneo (writes) / Emarsys | Queue and retry silently; never block the user flow |
| Omneo (reads) | **Load-bearing for My Account profile pages** — per DMU-004 only email + Omneo ID are migrated; all other customer profile data is sourced live from Omneo at login. Surface an explicit retry/error UI on profile pages if the round-trip fails; do not render stale or partial profile data. |
| Google Maps | Degrade to manual address entry; never hard-block checkout |
| AP21 (Retail Rewards) | On AP21 unavailability at the point of Rewards application, inform the customer and allow an alternative payment method |
| Narvar (EDD) | Suppress widget; do not show an error or block checkout |

### 12.1 Blast-Radius Containment

The failure modes above describe what the PWA does when a single integration is unavailable. This section covers how to limit the *spread* of an attack or outage — ensuring a degraded integration cannot consume shared resources and take down unrelated features.

#### Edge (outside the PWA — Infrastructure / SI Partner)

* **Web Application Firewalls + rate limiting** is the primary lever for volumetric attacks and credential-stuffing.
* **SFCC Business Manager** provides API-level rate limiting for SFCC endpoints, independent of the storefront edge.

#### SSR layer (inside the PWA)

`overrides/app/ssr.js` makes server-side `fetch` calls directly (token exchange, JWKS, SF Payments metadata). Node's native `fetch` is backed by `undici` internally. Undici's `dispatcher` option (the per-call `dispatcher` option on individual `fetch()` invocations) allows each upstream origin to be given its own connection pool with an independent cap. This prevents a slow or flooded integration (e.g. checkout APIs) from exhausting connections for unrelated origins (e.g. Contentful, JWKS).

> **Implementation note:** the per-call `dispatcher` option is safer than the `setGlobalDispatcher` in a managed environment (MRT) since it does not touch the global dispatcher that Salesforce internal libraries may rely on. The `commerce-sdk-react` hooks manage their own HTTP client server-side (Commerce SDK) and are not affected in either approach.

The connection pool split is an engineering decision — the right pool boundaries and sizes depend on observed traffic patterns and the integration map in §7. Planned pools (connection caps should be validated later — see §9.3):

| Pool | Origin | Calls | Cap | `connectTimeout` | `bodyTimeout` | Reasoning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sfcc-scapi` | `<https://{shortCode}.api.commercecloud.salesforce.com`> | SLAS JWKS (token validation for passwordless login, reset password) | 5 | 5 s | 8 s | `jose` caches the JWK set for its rotation period; actual network calls are rare. Isolated so a JWKS fetch is never starved by higher-volume pools. |
| `sfcc-payments` | `config.app.sfPayments.metadataUrl` host (a `*.demandware.net` or SCAPI hostname — waiting confirmation from Mani) | Payment method metadata on every checkout page SSR | 10 | 5 s | 8 s | Called on every checkout page load; moderate frequency. Separate from `sfcc-scapi` because a checkout traffic spike must not consume SLAS connections. |
| `mulesoft` | `MULESOFT_BASE_URL` | Order history, order details, boutique / BOPIS stock check, GiveX balance check | 20 | 5 s | 10 s | Highest user-facing concurrency (My Account + PDP). GiveX balance calls carry payment credentials in the POST body — a slow MuleSoft response must not hold connections open and starve other pools. Highest cap reflects the broadest call surface. |

---

13. Testing Strategy
--------------------

Three layers, no duplicated coverage — the cheapest layer that proves a behaviour wins.

| Layer | Tool | Covers |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Unit | Vitest | Pure logic, data mapping, transforms, isolated hooks |
| Component interaction | Storybook `play` | Single-component user interactions |
| E2E | Playwright | Full journeys, multi-region, integration boundaries |

### 13.1 What is tested

Failure paths that would be non-obvious or costly to debug: Contentful → component data mapping, locale / currency transforms, Global-e pricing / tax branching, checkout ownership, consent gating, cart mutations, optimistic-update rollback. Framework behaviour and pure visual rendering are not tested at this layer.

### 13.2 E2E gherkin-first workflow

Every Playwright spec starts as a Gherkin `.feature` file that Lead QA validates in plain English before any code is written. This prevents technically correct tests of the wrong behaviour.

### 13.3 Multi-region fixtures

E2E specs are parameterised by `SITE_ID` from day one — every journey runs across all 8 storefronts and 11 active locales, with site-specific `baseUrl`, currency, checkout owner, tax model, and consent default supplied by a fixture rather than hardcoded. (Because a test hardcoded to one region cannot be cheaply expanded later)

### 13.4 Selector priority

Tests select elements the way users and assistive tech perceive them: accessible selectors (role + name, label, visible text) first, semantic HTML attributes second (`alt`, `title`), `data-testid` only when nothing semantic applies. Tag/class/DOM-position selectors are not used. This doubles as a continuous accessibility check.

---

14. CI/CD & Environments
------------------------

This section probably belong to a DevOps TSD, but will put here temporarily until we have one.

### 14.1 Topology

A six-tier environment topology spans **Local → Dev → SIT → Stage → UAT → Prod**. Each tier (other than Local) has its own SFCC realm, Contentful environment, and MuleSoft connections. Ownership splits across three zones — Digital, IT/NewStore, and Shared (Digital + Business).

| # | Tier | Owner | Purpose | Third-party availability | Deploy trigger |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | **Local** | Digital | Feature build on developer machines | All services mocked (MSW stubs) | `npm start` |
| 2 | **Dev** | Digital | Integrated digital testing across all 6 storefronts, independent of NewStore | MuleSoft STG · NewStore Dev · Omneo STG · Narvar stub · Adyen sandbox | Merge to `develop` |
| 3 | **SIT** | IT / NewStore | NewStore SIT and regression on its own cadence | NewStore STG · MuleSoft STG · Narvar STG · AP21 test | NewStore release cadence (parallel lane, non-blocking for Digital releases) |
| 4 | **Stage** (E2E) | Shared | End-to-end testing with all third parties live; time-boxed booked windows | NewStore STG · MuleSoft STG · Omneo STG · Narvar STG · Adyen sandbox | Booked 2-week window |
| 5 | **UAT** | Shared | Business acceptance across all 6 regions | NewStore STG · Narvar STG · Omneo STG · Adyen sandbox | Business approval gate |
| 6 | **Prod** | Live | Production; AU canary then flag-flip to remaining regions | NewStore PROD · MuleSoft PROD · Omneo PROD · Narvar PROD · Adyen PROD | Release manager + canary gate |

Stage is the **contractual performance-test environment** referenced in §9.3 — it mirrors production infrastructure (same MRT bundle class, CDN/edge configuration, SFCC realm tier).

### 14.2 Branch model

GitFlow with explicit back-merges to keep `develop` aligned with production.

| Branch | Branched from | Merges to |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `feature/*` | `develop` | `develop` |
| `fix/*` | `develop` | `develop` |
| `release/*` | `develop` | `main` **and** `develop` |
| `fix/release-{version}-*` | the `release/*` branch | the `release/*` branch (forward-merged to `develop` via the release back-merge) |
| `hotfix/*` | `main` | `main` **and** `develop` |
| `develop`, `main` | — | protected; PR-only |

Release branches are supervised — code logic fixes go on a `fix/release-{version}-*` sub-branch rather than directly on the release branch. Releases and hotfixes always back-merge to `develop` so production fixes flow forward automatically.

### 14.3 CI workflows

**QA workflow (**`qa.yml`) — runs on every PR to `develop` and `release/**`. Code-correctness checks with no environment dependency:

* Unit tests (Vitest)
* Storybook interaction tests (`play` functions) and component-level accessibility checks via `@storybook/addon-a11y` (`storybook test --ci`)

**SIT gate (**`digital-sit.yml`) — runs on push/PR to `release/**`; on merge to `develop` it also deploys to the **Dev** environment (tier 2 in §14.1). Environment-dependent checks:

* Playwright `p0` priority specs
* Bundle-size check against the ceilings in §9
* Contract tests against the MuleSoft OpenAPI specification
* Lighthouse CI thresholds (Performance ≥ 0.80, Accessibility ≥ 0.90, Best Practices ≥ 0.90)
* Trend gate against the LHCI history server

### 14.4 Deployment

Deployment is via Salesforce Managed Runtime. Each tier maps to its own MRT target:

* **Dev** — deployed on merge to `develop`, gated on a clean SIT gate (§14.3)
* **SIT** — deployed on the NewStore release cadence, isolated from the Digital release path (failures do not block `release/**`)
* **Stage** — deployed on a booked 2-week window for full end-to-end testing with live third parties
* **UAT** — deployed for business acceptance; promotion requires Business sign-off
* **Prod** — release-manager-gated; AU canary first, then flag-flip to remaining regions

Production deploys are gated on a clean SIT gate run plus stakeholder approval through Stage and UAT.

 379: * **Images:** all storefront imagery — product and editorial — is stored in and served from **Contentful** (`images.ctfassets.net`) via the Contentful Images API; SFCC holds no image assets (DMU-010 migration de-scoped; product images CRM-075; all media via the CMS library HPC-003). The PWA generates `srcset` / `sizes` and sets size, quality, and format per breakpoint on the asset URL — **AVIF primary with WebP / JPEG fallbacks**. Lazy-load all non-LCP images; priority-load the primary hero image (PRD-064). Never render full-resolution images at thumbnail size.
 383:   + **Content-managed page videos → Contentful** by default, served from the Contentful asset CDN and referenced within the CMS content entry alongside the page content. Editorial pages may also embed a Vimeo video by URL where preferred (HPC-004) — the product/editorial split above is the expected pattern, not a hard restriction.
 431: * Localised privacy policy pages, served from Contentful per storefront.
 462: | Contentful | Render page without editorial content; never block commerce data on CMS |
 482: `overrides/app/ssr.js` makes server-side `fetch` calls directly (token exchange, JWKS, SF Payments metadata). Node's native `fetch` is backed by `undici` internally. Undici's `dispatcher` option (the per-call `dispatcher` option on individual `fetch()` invocations) allows each upstream origin to be given its own connection pool with an independent cap. This prevents a slow or flooded integration (e.g. checkout APIs) from exhausting connections for unrelated origins (e.g. Contentful, JWKS).
 494: | `marketing-cloud-rest` | `<https://{subdomain}.rest.marketingcloudapis.com`> | Magic-link email send (passwordless login, reset password) | 5 | 5 s | 15 s | Same trigger as above; higher body timeout because email delivery APIs can respond slowly under load. |
 498: **Contentful:** The Contentful SDK (`contentful` v11) does not expose a `dispatcher` hook on its internal fetch calls, so connection isolation for Contentful is not achievable through this pattern. Primary mitigation is the graceful degradation rule in §12 (Render page without editorial content).
 515: Failure paths that would be non-obvious or costly to debug: Contentful → component data mapping, locale / currency transforms, Global-e pricing / tax branching, checkout ownership, consent gating, cart mutations, optimistic-update rollback. Framework behaviour and pure visual rendering are not tested at this layer.

> **Status:** 🟡 In progress · **Owner:** Jhoan Rose Dela Cruz · **Reporter:** Jasmijn Tsang · **Epic:** [SFCC-1 Platform Setup & Environments](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-1) · **Updated:** 2026-07-22
> **Audience:** the incoming Contentful squad (briefing artefact) plus Squad A engineers building the SFCC-side connection.
> **Provenance:** seeded from the SFCC-123 template and fact-checked against the codebase, Confluence, and the linked Jira stories on 2026-07-22. Items still unconfirmed are called out as open, never asserted as fact.

---

## 0. Purpose & scope [Task-5 framing]

**Problem this TSD solves:** give the incoming Contentful squad, and Squad A, a single briefing that pins down the Contentful-to-SFCC integration pattern, the content model SFCC must consume, locale setup, and the SFCC-side build scope, so the two teams share one boundary before the dedicated Contentful squad onboards.

- **In scope:** SFCC/MRT-side integration design, content-model requirements SFCC must consume, locale configuration, and the Accenture-vs-Contentful-squad handoff boundary.
- **Out of scope:** the full Contentful setup owned by the incoming squad (content authoring, Studio operations, the separate Contentful SOW). Linked, not specified here.

Contentful is the sole CMS across all Zimmermann storefronts (HPC-001): editorial modules, banners, size-guide fallback content, promotional content, and global assets. SFCC owns all commerce data; Contentful owns editorial. This spike is the same work item tracked as Open Item #3 ("Define Contentful content model and connector customisation scope") on [TSD: Product, SFCC Catalogue & Data Integration](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/292061208). Ticket: [SFCC-123](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-123).

## 1. Integration architecture & data flow [DoD-1 · Task-1]

**Target pattern** (per [`.docs/integration/02-contentful.md`](../integration/02-contentful.md) §3-§5 and [Technical Solution Design, PWA](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/256835585) §7): Contentful to MRT (Node/SSR) to browser, SSR-first for SEO and LCP.

```
PWA (SSR, then CSR hydration)
   ├──► Contentful Delivery API (CDA)      published content, SSR + browser; public token, safe in bundle
   ├──► Contentful Preview API (CPA)        drafts, MRT proxy only; token server-side, never in browser
   ├──► Contentful Images API               images.ctfassets.net, srcset/sizes, AVIF then WebP fallback
   ├──► GraphQL Content API                 composed pages, one request, field-projected
   └──◄  Publish webhook → MRT /webhooks/contentful   HMAC-verified; clears SSR cache keys
```

| Surface | Origin / boundary | Token | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| CDA (published) | Browser + SSR | `CONTENTFUL_DELIVERY_TOKEN` (public, read-only) | SSR-first target; held as an MRT env var so rotation is centralised |
| CPA (drafts) | MRT proxy only | `CONTENTFUL_PREVIEW_TOKEN` (server-side) | Studio live preview via iframe `postMessage` |
| CMA (schema sync) | CI / local only | `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN` | Never in MRT or the bundle; build-time only |
| Publish webhook | Contentful to MRT | `CMS_WEBHOOK_SECRET` (HMAC) | Cache purge; 60s SWR TTL fallback |

CDN limit: 55 uncached requests per second per CDA token, absorbed by the SSR cache. Single Contentful Space, one environment per delivery tier (see §4).

> **Current implementation vs target (verified in code).** The live data layer is [`overrides/app/hooks/useContentful.ts`](../../overrides/app/hooks/useContentful.ts): two hooks (`useContentfulEntry`, `useContentfulEntries`) that fetch **browser-side over REST** from `cdn.contentful.com` (CDA) or `preview.contentful.com` (CPA) with `include=2` to resolve linked assets. Config comes from [`overrides/app/config/contentful.ts`](../../overrides/app/config/contentful.ts) via `getConfig()`. The **SSR-first fetch, the GraphQL Content API, and the publish-webhook receiver are documented as the target but are not yet in the code** (see §3 and §6, items 3 and 10). This is deliberate build scope, not a defect, but the briefing should not imply SSR editorial is live today.

# TSD: Contentful Integration, SFCC-Side Design & Content Model (SFCC-123)

> **Status:** 🟡 In progress · **Owner:** Jhoan Rose Dela Cruz · **Reporter:** Jasmijn Tsang · **Epic:** [SFCC-1 Platform Setup & Environments](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-1) · **Updated:** 2026-07-22
> **Audience:** the incoming Contentful squad (briefing artefact) plus Squad A engineers building the SFCC-side connection.
> **Provenance:** seeded from the SFCC-123 template and fact-checked against the codebase, Confluence, and the linked Jira stories on 2026-07-22. Items still unconfirmed are called out as open, never asserted as fact.

---

## 0. Purpose & scope [Task-5 framing]

**Problem this TSD solves:** give the incoming Contentful squad, and Squad A, a single briefing that pins down the Contentful-to-SFCC integration pattern, the content model SFCC must consume, locale setup, and the SFCC-side build scope, so the two teams share one boundary before the dedicated Contentful squad onboards.

- **In scope:** SFCC/MRT-side integration design, content-model requirements SFCC must consume, locale configuration, and the Accenture-vs-Contentful-squad handoff boundary.
- **Out of scope:** the full Contentful setup owned by the incoming squad (content authoring, Studio operations, the separate Contentful SOW). Linked, not specified here.

Contentful is the sole CMS across all Zimmermann storefronts (HPC-001): editorial modules, banners, size-guide fallback content, promotional content, and global assets. SFCC owns all commerce data; Contentful owns editorial. This spike is the same work item tracked as Open Item #3 ("Define Contentful content model and connector customisation scope") on [TSD: Product, SFCC Catalogue & Data Integration](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/292061208). Ticket: [SFCC-123](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-123).

## 1. Integration architecture & data flow [DoD-1 · Task-1]

**Target pattern** (per [`.docs/integration/02-contentful.md`](../integration/02-contentful.md) §3-§5 and [Technical Solution Design, PWA](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/256835585) §7): Contentful to MRT (Node/SSR) to browser, SSR-first for SEO and LCP.

```
PWA (SSR, then CSR hydration)
   ├──► Contentful Delivery API (CDA)      published content, SSR + browser; public token, safe in bundle
   ├──► Contentful Preview API (CPA)        drafts, MRT proxy only; token server-side, never in browser
   ├──► Contentful Images API               images.ctfassets.net, srcset/sizes, AVIF then WebP fallback
   ├──► GraphQL Content API                 composed pages, one request, field-projected
   └──◄  Publish webhook → MRT /webhooks/contentful   HMAC-verified; clears SSR cache keys
```

| Surface | Origin / boundary | Token | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| CDA (published) | Browser + SSR | `CONTENTFUL_DELIVERY_TOKEN` (public, read-only) | SSR-first target; held as an MRT env var so rotation is centralised |
| CPA (drafts) | MRT proxy only | `CONTENTFUL_PREVIEW_TOKEN` (server-side) | Studio live preview via iframe `postMessage` |
| CMA (schema sync) | CI / local only | `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN` | Never in MRT or the bundle; build-time only |
| Publish webhook | Contentful to MRT | `CMS_WEBHOOK_SECRET` (HMAC) | Cache purge; 60s SWR TTL fallback |

CDN limit: 55 uncached requests per second per CDA token, absorbed by the SSR cache. Single Contentful Space, one environment per delivery tier (see §4).

> **Current implementation vs target (verified in code).** The live data layer is [`overrides/app/hooks/useContentful.ts`](../../overrides/app/hooks/useContentful.ts): two hooks (`useContentfulEntry`, `useContentfulEntries`) that fetch **browser-side over REST** from `cdn.contentful.com` (CDA) or `preview.contentful.com` (CPA) with `include=2` to resolve linked assets. Config comes from [`overrides/app/config/contentful.ts`](../../overrides/app/config/contentful.ts) via `getConfig()`. The **SSR-first fetch, the GraphQL Content API, and the publish-webhook receiver are documented as the target but are not yet in the code** (see §3 and §6, items 3 and 10). This is deliberate build scope, not a defect, but the briefing should not imply SSR editorial is live today.

## 2. Content model requirements [DoD-2 · Task-2]

**What exists in code today (verified):**

- **Studio Experiences** (drag-and-drop, registered via `@contentful/experiences-sdk-react` in [`experiences/definitions.ts`](../../overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/definitions.ts), autogenerated from the `.tsx` sources): `collection-hero`, `image-text`, `shoppable-image`.
- **CDA content type as schema-as-code** ([`scripts/contentful/content-types/`](../../scripts/contentful/content-types/)): only `shoppableImage`. Registered in `CONTENT_TYPE_IDS` in [`contentfulMapping.ts`](../../overrides/app/config/contentfulMapping.ts).
- **Editorial React components without a confirmed content type**: `heroBanner`, `duplexSection`, `videoEmbed`, `productHero` ([`components/contentful/index.ts`](../../overrides/app/components/contentful/index.ts)).

Contentful integration is not a separate sprint: per [`.docs/memory/sprintScope.md`](../memory/sprintScope.md), "Contentful works/integration will be done as part of each corresponding functional story." Sprint columns below follow the functional-area schedule (today is Sprint 2, 13-24 Jul).

| Content type | Purpose | Sprint | Exists in code? | Backing story (status) | SFCC component |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Collection hero | Homepage / campaign hero | 1-2 | ✅ Studio Exp `collection-hero` | [SFCC-90](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-90) (In Refinement) | `experiences/collectionHero.tsx` |
| Image + text block | Editorial image + text | 1-2 | ✅ Studio Exp `image-text` | [SFCC-90](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-90) | `experiences/imageText.tsx` |
| Shoppable image | Shop-the-look, product hotspots | 1-2 | ✅ Studio Exp + CDA type `shoppableImage` | [SFCC-90](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-90) | `experiences/shoppableImage.tsx` |
| Homepage modules | Hero banner, featured tiles, campaign links, top categories, editorial/boutique duo | 1-2 | Partial: `heroBanner.tsx`, `duplexSection.tsx` (no confirmed content type) | [SFCC-90](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-90) (In Refinement) | `components/contentful/{heroBanner,duplexSection}.tsx` |

| PLP inline grid insert | Campaign image / image+text / featured tile insert | 2-3 | ❌ | UI [SFCC-190](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-190) (To Do) · content [SFCC-204](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-204) (To Do) | to build |

| SEO FAQ / Article schema | JSON-LD structured data authored in Contentful | Backlog (Enhancements) | ❌ | [SFCC-173](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-173) (To Do) | to build |
| (existing, unmapped) | `productHero`, `videoEmbed` components exist without a confirmed content type | — | ✅ component only | — | `components/contentful/{productHero,videoEmbed}.tsx` |

**Field reference (verified):**

- `shoppableImage` CDA type: `title` (Symbol, required), `image` (Asset link, required), `imageAlt` (Symbol), `hotspots` (Object; shape `[{ x: 0-100, y: 0-100, productId: "<SFCC master product ID>" }]`). The `productId` key is fixed by `SFCC_PRODUCT_ID_FIELD` in `contentfulMapping.ts`.
- Studio Experience `shoppable-image` stores `hotspots` as a JSON **Text** variable (versus the CDA type's `Object`); worth reconciling to one representation when the model is formalised.
- Studio Experience variables: `collection-hero` (headline, subheadline, ctaLabel, ctaUrl, backgroundImage/Media); `image-text` (image/Media, imageAlt, headline, body, imagePosition default `left`).

For each **required** type still to build, the incoming squad and Squad A must agree the field set and which fields are localised (`localized: true`) versus structural (`localized: false`, e.g. asset links and product IDs). Schema-as-code lives at `scripts/contentful/content-types/*.js`; Studio Experience definitions are generated from `overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/*.tsx` via `npm run generate:contentful`.

## 3. SFCC-side consumption & build scope [DoD-4 · Task-3]

**Already built (verified against the tree):**

- **Config / types:** `overrides/app/config/contentful.ts`, `config/contentfulMapping.ts` + `contentfulMapping.generated.ts` (`SUPPORTED_LOCALES`, `SITE_LOCALES`, `CONTENTFUL_ENVIRONMENTS`, `CONTENT_TYPE_IDS`, `SFCC_PRODUCT_ID_FIELD`), `types/contentful.ts`.
- **Data hooks:** `overrides/app/hooks/useContentful.ts` (`useContentfulEntry`, `useContentfulEntries`; REST CDA/CPA with linked-asset resolution).
- **Editorial components:** `components/contentful/{heroBanner, duplexSection, videoEmbed, productHero}.tsx`.
- **Studio Experiences:** `components/contentful/experiences/{collectionHero, imageText, shoppableImage, hotspotPopup, hotspotMarker}.tsx` + `definitions.ts`; route `overrides/app/pages/experience/index.tsx`.
- **Schema-as-code + tooling:** `scripts/contentful/{sync.js, generateDefinitions.mjs, migrations/001-initial-content-types.mjs, setup/{bootstrapSpace, getConfig, runMigrations, promoteAlias, detectDrift}.mjs}`, `content-types/shoppableImage.js`.
- **Runtime + governance:** `overrides/app/ssr/contentSecurityPolicy.ts` (CSP allowances), Studio registration via the `contentful-register-component` skill, a CI `contentful-drift-audit`, and a Husky pre-commit content-type drift check.
- **Locale source of truth:** `config/sites.overlay.js` + `config/sites.generated.js` + `contentfulMapping.generated.ts`, regenerated in one pass via `npm run sync:regional-config` (see §4).

| Capability | APIs / fields consumed | Rendering logic | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Studio Experiences (collection-hero, image-text, shoppable-image) | Experiences SDK; variables per definition | Registered components rendered by the experience route | **Built** |
| Shoppable-image hotspots to SFCC product | `productId` per hotspot to SCAPI shopper-products | Marker + popup resolve product client-side | **Built** (component); depends on live SCAPI product data |
| Homepage modules content-managed | CDA entries to hero/duplex components | Component mapping | Components partial; content model **to build** (SFCC-90) |

## 4. Locale configuration [DoD-3 · Task-4]

**Resolved.** The earlier "locale count" conflict was a category error, not a data conflict:

- **8 SFCC sites / storefront catalogues** (Business Manager view): AU, UK, US, USIntl, EU, EUIntl, HK, ME. The EU site alone carries 5 locales. This is the "8 storefronts" figure in [SFCC-151](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-151) and the Product TSD §5.
- **10 PWA sites, 9 distinct Contentful locales** (`config/sites.overlay.js`, verified): EU domestic is one SFCC site split into four single-locale PWA sites. Distinct locales = `en` (default), `en-US`, `en-GB`, `fr`, `it`, `es`, `en-CH`, `en-HK`, `en-AE`. This matches the "9 locales" on the ops page and `DEFAULT_LOCALE = 'en'` in `contentfulMapping.ts`.

Translatable fields use `localized: true`; structural fields (asset links, product IDs) use `localized: false`. Locales are created in the `master` environment at bootstrap and inherited by cloned environments. SFCC-123 "Spike: Contentful Integration Technical Design & Content Model" — Jira **Spike**, project SFCC (zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net), label Squad-A, High, **In Progress**. Parent epic **SFCC-1** (Platform Setup & Environments). **Assignee: Jhoan Rose Dela Cruz**; reporter Jasmijn Tsang. Created 2026-07-08. Sibling spikes: SFCC-121/122 (see [[sfcc-122]]). Board house style Objective/Background/Tasks/DoD (see [[f2r-spike]]).

Objective: document the Contentful→MRT→SFCC integration + data flow, define Sprint 1/2 content types, define what SFCC consumes (APIs, fields, rendering), locale config across the storefronts, and the Accenture-vs-incoming-Contentful-squad handoff boundary. DoD: a TSD briefing artefact for the incoming Contentful squad.

Ticket timeline: 2026-07-21 Jhoan posted first draft `Contentful Integration TSD_SFCC123.docx`; 2026-07-21 Marcel attached `tsd-integration-template.md`; 2026-07-22 Marcel handed Jhoan a spike-specific TSD skeleton `sfcc-123-contentful-integration-tsd.md` seeded from repo/Confluence/Jira. **These are Jira attachments, NOT in the repo** (no `.docs/spikes/SFCC-123-*.md` yet — unlike SFCC-122 which lives at `zimmermann-pwa/.docs/spikes/SFCC-122-mrt-api-capabilities.md`).

**Crux/reframe (same shape as [[sfcc-122]]):** the SFCC-side Contentful integration is already substantially BUILT & documented, not greenfield discovery. Codebase `zimmermann-pwa`: `scripts/contentful/` (sync.js, migrations/, setup/ bootstrapSpace+getConfig+runMigrations+promoteAlias+detectDrift, generateDefinitions.mjs), `overrides/app/components/contentful/` (heroBanner, duplexSection, productHero, videoEmbed) + `experiences/` (collectionHero, imageText, shoppableImage, hotspotPopup/Marker), `hooks/useContentful.ts`, config/contentful.ts + contentfulMapping(.generated).ts, types/contentful.ts, `.claude/skills/contentful-register-component`, CI contentful-drift-audit + Husky pre-commit drift check. Deps: contentful, contentful-management, contentful-cli, @contentful/experiences-sdk-react, @contentful/live-preview. Integration doc: `.docs/integration/02-contentful.md` (CDA/CPA/CMA split, publish webhook→MRT cache purge, SSR-first+GraphQL, Images API, failure modes). Architecture: single Contentful Space, one env per delivery tier.

Open gaps/discrepancies to resolve in the TSD: (a) locale/storefront count inconsistent — ticket "8 storefronts", Confluence Setup page "9 locales" (lists 10 storefronts), `02-contentful.md §7` says "Eleven" but lists 10; reconcile vs `config/sites.js`. (b) Only ONE editorial content type codified (`shoppableImage`) + 3 Studio Experiences (CollectionHero/ImageText/ShoppableImage) — content model still to build. (c) Ownership table (`02-contentful.md §1`) marks PLP/PDP editorial split, mega-menu promo tiles, category-landing routing as *pending*. (d) Human setup checklist incomplete: MRT env vars per tier, Contentful→MRT cache-purge webhook, Contentful roles, CI CMA GitHub secret. (e) **Hard blocker** (Confluence 268337165): Contentful must provide per-env credentials (Space ID, CDA/CPA tokens, webhook secret) — storefront can't connect without them.

Key Confluence (space SFCC): 318472193 "Contentful CMS — Setup & Operations" (v7, ops runbook: 6-tier env topology, alias/release workflow, token matrix, locales, content types, drift, scripts, checklist), 292061208 (TSD Product), 303890433 (Third Party Integrations — App Exchange connector + Delivery API), 257327107 (PDP editorial blocks), 303104002 (Regional Storefronts/locales), 268337165 (Third Party Credentials — blocker), 258408463 (Decision Log — images Contentful vs SFCC), 303071234 (Homepage & Content model/authoring), 257163278 (Product — content-type open questions).

input.new_string: Key findings (verified 2026-07-22): (a) **Locale RESOLVED** — not a data conflict, a category error: 8 SFCC sites/storefront catalogues (EU carries 5 locales), 10 PWA sites (EU domestic split into en/fr/it/es single-locale PWA sites), 9 distinct Contentful locales (`en` default, en-US, en-GB, fr, it, es, en-CH, en-HK, en-AE) per `config/sites.overlay.js` + `contentfulMapping.ts`. `02-contentful.md §7`'s "Eleven" is WRONG (wrongly includes `en-AU` = BM site default the AU PWA overrides to `en`, plus a separate `en (EU)`); fix §7 to 9 — pending. (c) **Current code vs documented target diverges:** live data layer `overrides/app/hooks/useContentful.ts` is a BROWSER-SIDE REST fetch (CDA/CPA, include=2); the SSR-first fetch, GraphQL Content API, and publish-webhook receiver described in `02-contentful.md §3`/PWA TSD §7 are NOT yet built. (e) Ownership (`02-contentful.md §1`) marks PLP/PDP editorial split, mega-menu promo tiles, category-landing routing *pending*. (f) Human setup checklist incomplete: MRT env vars per tier, Contentful→MRT cache-purge webhook, Contentful roles, CI CMA GitHub secret. (g) **Hard blocker** (Confluence 268337165): Contentful must provide per-env credentials (Space ID, CDA/CPA tokens, webhook secret). +- **State of play:** the integration is substantially scaffolded (config, data hooks, Studio Experiences, schema-as-code tooling, CSP, CI drift checks), but the SSR-first fetch, the GraphQL Content API, the publish-webhook receiver, and most editorial content types are still to build.
+- **Content model today:** one CDA content type (`shoppableImage`) plus three Studio Experiences (`collection-hero`, `image-text`, `shoppable-image`). Everything else in §2 is to build.
+- **Locale:** 8 SFCC sites, 10 PWA sites, 9 Contentful locales (`en` default). The earlier count conflict is resolved (§4).
+- **Hard blocker:** Contentful must provide per-environment credentials before the storefront can connect (§6 item 8).
+- **Read next:** §2 for content types by sprint, §3 for what SFCC consumes, §6 for what must be unblocked before onboarding.
## 0. Purpose & scope [Task-5 framing]

**Problem this TSD solves:** give the incoming Contentful squad, and Squad A, a single briefing that pins down the Contentful-to-SFCC integration pattern, the content model SFCC must consume, locale setup, and the SFCC-side build scope, so the two teams share one boundary before the dedicated Contentful squad onboards.

You are an independent, skeptical technical reviewer. Review a Technical Design Document against its Definition of Done and verify its factual claims against the codebase. Do NOT edit any files — read and report only. Do not rubber-stamp; your job is to find real gaps.

## The Definition of Done (from Jira SFCC-123)
"A technical design document is produced covering the Contentful integration architecture, content model requirements, locale setup, and SFCC-side build scope, ready to be shared with the incoming Contentful squad as a briefing artefact."

The ticket's six tasks: (1) document the Contentful → MRT → SFCC integration pattern and data flow; (2) identify which content types are required in Contentful for Sprint 1 and 2; (3) define what the SFCC side needs to consume (which APIs, which content-model fields, what rendering logic); (4) identify locale configuration aligned to the storefronts; (5) clarify the handoff boundary (what Accenture builds vs what the incoming Contentful squad owns); (6) flag blockers/dependencies before the Contentful squad onboards.

## Rubric — assess each PASS / GAP with specific evidence (quote the doc)
- A. Integration architecture & data flow at briefing altitude, current-vs-target distinguished
- B. Content types required for Sprint 1 AND Sprint 2 explicitly (not vague), with existence status + backing story
- C. SFCC-side consumption: APIs + content-model fields + rendering logic, per surface
- D. Locale config aligned to storefronts, code-verified, earlier count discrepancy resolved
- E. Handoff boundary (Accenture vs Contentful squad) explicit and unambiguous
- F. Blockers & dependencies with owner + status
- G. Briefing quality: has an at-a-glance summary, self-contained, lean (no bloat), consistent status/owner, NO em dashes (—) or en dashes (–) anywhere
- H. Factual accuracy: no unverified claim shipped as fact; no invented specifics

## Verify these code-level claims against the actual repo files (open them)
- `overrides/app/hooks/useContentful.ts` — is the live data layer browser-side REST against cdn/preview.contentful.com with include=2? Is there any SSR fetch, GraphQL, or webhook receiver here or nearby?
- `overrides/app/config/contentfulMapping.ts` — is `shoppableImage` the only entry in CONTENT_TYPE_IDS? Is DEFAULT_LOCALE 'en'? Are the tier environments (dev/test/sit/staging/uat/master) as the doc says?
- `overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/definitions.ts` — are exactly three Studio Experiences registered (collection-hero, image-text, shoppable-image) with the variables the doc lists?
- `overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/hotspotPopup.tsx` and `shoppableImage.tsx` — does the popup resolve productId via `useProduct` from `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` and render product image from SFCC DIS (`disBaseLink`)?
- `scripts/contentful/content-types/shoppableImage.js` — do the fields match the doc (title/image/imageAlt/hotspots)?
- `config/sites.overlay.js` — do the 10 PWA sites and 9 distinct locales (en, en-US, en-GB, fr, it, es, en-CH, en-HK, en-AE) match the doc's §4 table exactly?
- Confirm every internal markdown link target in §9 and inline (paths beginning `../`) actually exists on disk relative to the doc's location (`.docs/spikes/`).

Note: Confluence/Jira-sourced claims are out of your scope — treat those as already verified; focus on the rubric, internal consistency, and the code claims above.

## Output
1. A rubric table: criterion → PASS/GAP → one-line evidence.
2. A ranked list of findings (most severe first): for each, the exact location/quote, why it's a problem, and a concrete fix. Separate "must-fix for DoD" from "nice-to-have".
3. Any factual discrepancy between the doc and the code, with the file:line evidence.
4. A final verdict: does the doc meet the DoD as-is, or what specifically blocks it.

---

# Independent Review: SFCC-123 Contentful Integration TSD

## 1. Rubric assessment

| # | Criterion | Verdict | Evidence (one line) |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | Integration architecture & data flow, current-vs-target distinguished | **PASS** | §1 has target diagram + surface/token table, then a "Current implementation vs target (verified in code)" callout. Code confirms browser-side REST only; no SSR/GraphQL/webhook found anywhere in repo. |
| B | Content types for Sprint 1 AND Sprint 2, explicit, with existence status + backing story | **PASS** (minor consistency snag) | §2 prose gives an explicit S1 vs S2 split; table adds "Exists in code?" + backing story with Jira status. Snag: table's `Sprint` column uses ranges (`1-2`, `2-3`) that don't line up with the crisp prose split, and `2-3` implies an undefined Sprint 3. |
| C | SFCC-side consumption: APIs + fields + rendering logic, per surface | **PASS** | §3 "Already built" list + capability table (APIs/fields, rendering logic, status) per surface, all matching the tree. |
| D | Locale config aligned to storefronts, code-verified, earlier count discrepancy resolved | **PASS** (one unverifiable figure) | §4 table matches `sites.overlay.js` and `contentfulMapping.generated.ts` exactly (10 PWA sites, 9 locales, `en` default); count conflict explicitly resolved. The "EU site alone carries 5 locales" line is not code-verifiable (see finding 3). |
| E | Handoff boundary explicit and unambiguous | **PASS** | §5 table splits Accenture vs Contentful squad per concern. One row (composed pages) is openly "pending, see §6 item 7" rather than settled, but that is flagged as a blocker, not hidden. |
| F | Blockers & dependencies with owner + status | **PASS** | §6: 10 items, each with owner + status; hard blocker (item 8, credentials) surfaced in At-a-glance. |
| G | Briefing quality: at-a-glance, self-contained, lean, consistent, NO em/en dashes | **PASS** | "At a glance" section present; self-contained; zero em/en dashes confirmed by scan. Minor redundancy across §2/§5/§6/§8 (see finding 4). |
| H | Factual accuracy: no unverified claim as fact, no invented specifics | **PASS** (one minor imprecision) | All code specifics verified true. One imprecise accessor name (finding 1); the "5 EU locales" figure (finding 3) is attributed to a Confluence/BM source, so not a fabrication. |

**No criterion fails.** All findings below are polish, not DoD blockers.

## 2. Ranked findings

### Must-fix for DoD
None. The document satisfies every clause of the DoD and the six ticket tasks.

### Nice-to-have (ranked)

**1. Minor factual imprecision: `getConfig()` accessor name (§1, line 51).**
The doc says "Config comes from `overrides/app/config/contentful.ts` via `getConfig()`." The runtime accessor the hooks actually call is **`getContentfulConfig()`** (`overrides/app/config/contentful.ts:19`; imported and called at `overrides/app/hooks/useContentful.ts:2,34`). `getConfig()` is the underlying PWA Kit `ssr-config` util that `contentful.ts` wraps internally (`contentful.ts:10,20`) — so the claim is defensible but reads as if the hook calls `getConfig()` directly.
*Fix:* change "via `getConfig()`" to "via `getContentfulConfig()`".

**2. Sprint column ranges conflict with the prose split (§2 table + §3 table).**
§2 prose is crisp: Sprint 1 = collection-hero, image-text, shoppable-image, homepage modules, promo announcement banner, global footer; Sprint 2 = PLP bottom-zone + inline grid insert + PDP size-guide; SEO FAQ = backlog. But the table's `Sprint` column shows `1-2`, `2-3`, etc. So the promo banner reads as "1-2" in the table yet "Sprint 1" in prose, and PLP types read "2-3" yet "Sprint 2" in prose. The `2-3` range also implies a Sprint 3 that is never defined. The doc already has a sentence explaining the value "is the range of the owning functional area," but the labels still read ambiguously against the prose.
*Fix:* set the table `Sprint` values to match the prose (`1` / `2` / `Backlog`), or drop the range column and rely on the prose split.

**3. "The EU site alone carries 5 locales" is not code-verifiable and superficially conflicts with the §4 table (§4, line 118).**
In the code layer, `ZimmermannEU` backs **4** single-locale PWA sites (`en-GB`, `fr`, `it`, `es`) — see `config/sites.overlay.js:37-40` and `contentfulMapping.generated.ts:13-16`. The doc's own §4 table also shows only 4 EU-backed rows. The "5 locales" figure is attributed to Business Manager / SFCC-151 (a Confluence source, out of my verification scope), but a reader comparing it to the 4 rows shown will see a 4-vs-5 discrepancy.
*Fix:* name the 5th EU locale or add a half-sentence that it is a BM-level locale not surfaced in the PWA overlay, so the figure reconciles with the table.

**4. Mild redundancy across sections (§2, §5, §6, §8).**
The hotspots-representation reconciliation appears in the §2 note *and* §8 item 2; composed-page ownership appears in §5, §6 item 7, *and* §8 item 3. Acceptable cross-referencing for a briefing, but it inflates length slightly.
*Fix (optional):* state each once and cross-reference, e.g. "(open question 2)".

## 3. Factual discrepancies (doc vs code)

Only one, and it is minor:

| Doc claim | Code reality | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| §1: "Config comes from ... via `getConfig()`" | The runtime accessor is `getContentfulConfig()`; `getConfig()` is the PWA Kit util it wraps | `overrides/app/config/contentful.ts:19` (`export const getContentfulConfig`), `:10` + `:20` (imports/calls `getConfig` from `@salesforce/pwa-kit-runtime`); `overrides/app/hooks/useContentful.ts:2,34` |

Everything else the doc asserts as code fact checks out exactly:
- `useContentful.ts` — two hooks, browser-side REST against `cdn.contentful.com`/`preview.contentful.com`, `include=2` (lines 43, 47, 106, 110). No SSR fetch, GraphQL, or webhook receiver anywhere in the repo (grep of `overrides`, `scripts` clean; only hits are a CSP allowlist and an unrelated pre-commit secret scanner).
- `contentfulMapping.ts` — `CONTENT_TYPE_IDS` = only `shoppableImage` (line 54); `DEFAULT_LOCALE = 'en'` (line 24); tier env map `dev/test/sit/staging/uat/production→master` (lines 39-46).
- `definitions.ts` — exactly three Studio Experiences (`collection-hero`, `image-text`, `shoppable-image`) with the exact variable sets the doc lists.
- `hotspotPopup.tsx` — resolves `productId` via `useProduct` from `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` (line 3, 12) and renders the SFCC product image from `disBaseLink` (line 27), name, price, PDP link.
- `shoppableImage.tsx` — parses `hotspots` JSON into `{x, y, productId}` markers (lines 18-35, 59-61).
- `content-types/shoppableImage.js` — fields `title`/`image`/`imageAlt`/`hotspots` match §2 exactly (Symbol req / Asset link req / Symbol / Object).
- `sites.overlay.js` — the 10 PWA sites and 9 distinct locales (`en, en-US, en-GB, fr, it, es, en-CH, en-HK, en-AE`) match §4's table row-for-row; `SUPPORTED_LOCALES` in `contentfulMapping.generated.ts:8` is the same 9.
- All 15 internal link targets in §9 and inline `../` paths exist on disk. Both cited npm scripts (`sync:regional-config`, `generate:contentful`) exist in `package.json` (lines 72, 84). CSP allowlist includes `images.ctfassets.net`, `cdn.contentful.com`, `preview.contentful.com` as the doc states.

## 4. Verdict

**The document meets the Definition of Done as-is.** It is a self-contained briefing artefact covering integration architecture and data flow, the content model by sprint with existence status and backing stories, SFCC-side consumption per surface, locale configuration aligned to the storefronts and code-verified, an explicit Accenture-vs-Contentful-squad handoff boundary, and a blockers list with owners and statuses. Current-vs-target is honestly distinguished, and the earlier locale-count conflict is resolved. No em/en dashes.

Nothing blocks sign-off. The four nice-to-have items are polish: correct `getConfig()` → `getContentfulConfig()` (finding 1), reconcile the Sprint-column ranges with the prose split (finding 2), and clarify or reconcile the "5 EU locales" figure (finding 3). I would not hold publication for any of them, though finding 1 is a quick, worthwhile correction since the briefing is going to an external squad.

# Independent Review: SFCC-123 Contentful Integration TSD

## 1. Rubric assessment

| # | Criterion | Verdict | Evidence (one line) |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | Integration architecture & data flow, current-vs-target distinguished | **PASS** | §1 has target diagram + surface/token table, then a "Current implementation vs target (verified in code)" callout. Code confirms browser-side REST only; no SSR/GraphQL/webhook found anywhere in repo. |
| B | Content types for Sprint 1 AND Sprint 2, explicit, with existence status + backing story | **PASS** (minor consistency snag) | §2 prose gives an explicit S1 vs S2 split; table adds "Exists in code?" + backing story with Jira status. Snag: table's `Sprint` column uses ranges (`1-2`, `2-3`) that don't line up with the crisp prose split, and `2-3` implies an undefined Sprint 3. |
| C | SFCC-side consumption: APIs + fields + rendering logic, per surface | **PASS** | §3 "Already built" list + capability table (APIs/fields, rendering logic, status) per surface, all matching the tree. |
| D | Locale config aligned to storefronts, code-verified, earlier count discrepancy resolved | **PASS** (one unverifiable figure) | §4 table matches `sites.overlay.js` and `contentfulMapping.generated.ts` exactly (10 PWA sites, 9 locales, `en` default); count conflict explicitly resolved. The "EU site alone carries 5 locales" line is not code-verifiable (see finding 3). |
| E | Handoff boundary explicit and unambiguous | **PASS** | §5 table splits Accenture vs Contentful squad per concern. One row (composed pages) is openly "pending, see §6 item 7" rather than settled, but that is flagged as a blocker, not hidden. |
| F | Blockers & dependencies with owner + status | **PASS** | §6: 10 items, each with owner + status; hard blocker (item 8, credentials) surfaced in At-a-glance. |
| G | Briefing quality: at-a-glance, self-contained, lean, consistent, NO em/en dashes | **PASS** | "At a glance" section present; self-contained; zero em/en dashes confirmed by scan. Minor redundancy across §2/§5/§6/§8 (see finding 4). |
| H | Factual accuracy: no unverified claim as fact, no invented specifics | **PASS** (one minor imprecision) | All code specifics verified true. One imprecise accessor name (finding 1); the "5 EU locales" figure (finding 3) is attributed to a Confluence/BM source, so not a fabrication. |

**No criterion fails.** All findings below are polish, not DoD blockers.

## 2. Ranked findings

### Must-fix for DoD
None. The document satisfies every clause of the DoD and the six ticket tasks.

### Nice-to-have (ranked)

**1. Minor factual imprecision: `getConfig()` accessor name (§1, line 51).**
The doc says "Config comes from `overrides/app/config/contentful.ts` via `getConfig()`." The runtime accessor the hooks actually call is **`getContentfulConfig()`** (`overrides/app/config/contentful.ts:19`; imported and called at `overrides/app/hooks/useContentful.ts:2,34`). `getConfig()` is the underlying PWA Kit `ssr-config` util that `contentful.ts` wraps internally (`contentful.ts:10,20`) — so the claim is defensible but reads as if the hook calls `getConfig()` directly.
*Fix:* change "via `getConfig()`" to "via `getContentfulConfig()`".

**2. Sprint column ranges conflict with the prose split (§2 table + §3 table).**
§2 prose is crisp: Sprint 1 = collection-hero, image-text, shoppable-image, homepage modules, promo announcement banner, global footer; Sprint 2 = PLP bottom-zone + inline grid insert + PDP size-guide; SEO FAQ = backlog. But the table's `Sprint` column shows `1-2`, `2-3`, etc. So the promo banner reads as "1-2" in the table yet "Sprint 1" in prose, and PLP types read "2-3" yet "Sprint 2" in prose. The `2-3` range also implies a Sprint 3 that is never defined. The doc already has a sentence explaining the value "is the range of the owning functional area," but the labels still read ambiguously against the prose.
*Fix:* set the table `Sprint` values to match the prose (`1` / `2` / `Backlog`), or drop the range column and rely on the prose split.

**3. "The EU site alone carries 5 locales" is not code-verifiable and superficially conflicts with the §4 table (§4, line 118).**
In the code layer, `ZimmermannEU` backs **4** single-locale PWA sites (`en-GB`, `fr`, `it`, `es`) — see `config/sites.overlay.js:37-40` and `contentfulMapping.generated.ts:13-16`. The doc's own §4 table also shows only 4 EU-backed rows. The "5 locales" figure is attributed to Business Manager / SFCC-151 (a Confluence source, out of my verification scope), but a reader comparing it to the 4 rows shown will see a 4-vs-5 discrepancy.
*Fix:* name the 5th EU locale or add a half-sentence that it is a BM-level locale not surfaced in the PWA overlay, so the figure reconciles with the table.

**4. Mild redundancy across sections (§2, §5, §6, §8).**
The hotspots-representation reconciliation appears in the §2 note *and* §8 item 2; composed-page ownership appears in §5, §6 item 7, *and* §8 item 3. Acceptable cross-referencing for a briefing, but it inflates length slightly.
*Fix (optional):* state each once and cross-reference, e.g. "(open question 2)".

## 3. Factual discrepancies (doc vs code)

Only one, and it is minor:

| Doc claim | Code reality | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| §1: "Config comes from ... via `getConfig()`" | The runtime accessor is `getContentfulConfig()`; `getConfig()` is the PWA Kit util it wraps | `overrides/app/config/contentful.ts:19` (`export const getContentfulConfig`), `:10` + `:20` (imports/calls `getConfig` from `@salesforce/pwa-kit-runtime`); `overrides/app/hooks/useContentful.ts:2,34` |

Everything else the doc asserts as code fact checks out exactly:
- `useContentful.ts` — two hooks, browser-side REST against `cdn.contentful.com`/`preview.contentful.com`, `include=2` (lines 43, 47, 106, 110). No SSR fetch, GraphQL, or webhook receiver anywhere in the repo (grep of `overrides`, `scripts` clean; only hits are a CSP allowlist and an unrelated pre-commit secret scanner).
- `contentfulMapping.ts` — `CONTENT_TYPE_IDS` = only `shoppableImage` (line 54); `DEFAULT_LOCALE = 'en'` (line 24); tier env map `dev/test/sit/staging/uat/production→master` (lines 39-46).
- `definitions.ts` — exactly three Studio Experiences (`collection-hero`, `image-text`, `shoppable-image`) with the exact variable sets the doc lists.
- `hotspotPopup.tsx` — resolves `productId` via `useProduct` from `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` (line 3, 12) and renders the SFCC product image from `disBaseLink` (line 27), name, price, PDP link.
- `shoppableImage.tsx` — parses `hotspots` JSON into `{x, y, productId}` markers (lines 18-35, 59-61).
- `content-types/shoppableImage.js` — fields `title`/`image`/`imageAlt`/`hotspots` match §2 exactly (Symbol req / Asset link req / Symbol / Object).
- `sites.overlay.js` — the 10 PWA sites and 9 distinct locales (`en, en-US, en-GB, fr, it, es, en-CH, en-HK, en-AE`) match §4's table row-for-row; `SUPPORTED_LOCALES` in `contentfulMapping.generated.ts:8` is the same 9.
- All 15 internal link targets in §9 and inline `../` paths exist on disk. Both cited npm scripts (`sync:regional-config`, `generate:contentful`) exist in `package.json` (lines 72, 84). CSP allowlist includes `images.ctfassets.net`, `cdn.contentful.com`, `preview.contentful.com` as the doc states.

## 4. Verdict

**The document meets the Definition of Done as-is.** It is a self-contained briefing artefact covering integration architecture and data flow, the content model by sprint with existence status and backing stories, SFCC-side consumption per surface, locale configuration aligned to the storefronts and code-verified, an explicit Accenture-vs-Contentful-squad handoff boundary, and a blockers list with owners and statuses. Current-vs-target is honestly distinguished, and the earlier locale-count conflict is resolved. No em/en dashes.

Nothing blocks sign-off. The four nice-to-have items are polish: correct `getConfig()` → `getContentfulConfig()` (finding 1), reconcile the Sprint-column ranges with the prose split (finding 2), and clarify or reconcile the "5 EU locales" figure (finding 3). I would not hold publication for any of them, though finding 1 is a quick, worthwhile correction since the briefing is going to an external squad.

29	## 1. Integration architecture & data flow [DoD-1 · Task-1]

31	**Target pattern** (per [`.docs/integration/02-contentful.md`](../integration/02-contentful.md) §3-§5 and [Technical Solution Design, PWA](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/256835585) §7): Contentful to MRT (Node/SSR) to browser, SSR-first for SEO and LCP.
32	
33	```
34	PWA (SSR, then CSR hydration)
35	   ├──► Contentful Delivery API (CDA)      published content, SSR + browser; public token, safe in bundle
36	   ├──► Contentful Preview API (CPA)        drafts, MRT proxy only; token server-side, never in browser
37	   ├──► Contentful Images API               images.ctfassets.net, srcset/sizes, AVIF then WebP fallback
38	   ├──► GraphQL Content API                 composed pages, one request, field-projected
39	   └──◄  Publish webhook → MRT /webhooks/contentful   HMAC-verified; clears SSR cache keys
40	```
41	
42	| Surface | Origin / boundary | Token | Notes |
43	|---|---|---|---|
44	| CDA (published) | Browser + SSR | `CONTENTFUL_DELIVERY_TOKEN` (public, read-only) | SSR-first target; held as an MRT env var so rotation is centralised |
45	| CPA (drafts) | MRT proxy only | `CONTENTFUL_PREVIEW_TOKEN` (server-side) | Studio live preview via iframe `postMessage` |
46	| CMA (schema sync) | CI / local only | `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN` | Never in MRT or the bundle; build-time only |
47	| Publish webhook | Contentful to MRT | `CMS_WEBHOOK_SECRET` (HMAC) | Cache purge; 60s SWR TTL fallback |
48	
49	CDN limit: 55 uncached requests per second per CDA token, absorbed by the SSR cache. Single Contentful Space, one environment per delivery tier (see §4).

Config comes from [`overrides/app/config/contentful.ts`](../../overrides/app/config/contentful.ts) via `getContentfulConfig()` (which wraps the PWA Kit `ssr-config` `getConfig()`). The **SSR-first fetch, the GraphQL Content API, and the publish-webhook receiver are documented as the target but are not yet in the code** (see §3 and §6, items 3 and 10). This is deliberate build scope, not a defect, but the briefing should not imply SSR editorial is live today.

# TSD: Contentful Integration, SFCC-Side Design & Content Model (SFCC-123)

> **Status:** 🟡 In progress · **Owner:** Jhoan Rose Dela Cruz · **Reporter:** Jasmijn Tsang · **Epic:** [SFCC-1 Platform Setup & Environments](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-1) · **Updated:** 2026-07-22
> **Audience:** the incoming Contentful squad (briefing artefact) plus Squad A engineers building the SFCC-side connection.
> **Provenance:** seeded from the SFCC-123 template and fact-checked against the codebase, Confluence, and the linked Jira stories on 2026-07-22. Items still unconfirmed are called out as open, never asserted as fact.

---

## At a glance

- **What this is:** the SFCC-side briefing for the incoming Contentful squad, covering integration architecture, the content model SFCC must consume, locale setup, and build scope. It is the work tracked as Open Item #3 on the Product TSD.
- **State of play:** the integration is substantially scaffolded (config, data hooks, Studio Experiences, schema-as-code tooling, CSP, CI drift checks), but the SSR-first fetch, the GraphQL Content API, the publish-webhook receiver, and most editorial content types are still to build.
- **Content model today:** one CDA content type (`shoppableImage`) plus three Studio Experiences (`collection-hero`, `image-text`, `shoppable-image`). Everything else in §2 is to build.
- **Locale:** 8 SFCC sites, 10 PWA sites, 9 Contentful locales (`en` default). The earlier count conflict is resolved (§4).
- **Hard blocker:** Contentful must provide per-environment credentials before the storefront can connect (§6 item 8).
- **Read next:** §2 for content types by sprint, §3 for what SFCC consumes, §6 for what must be unblocked before onboarding.

---

## 0. Purpose & scope [Task-5 framing]

**Problem this TSD solves:** give the incoming Contentful squad, and Squad A, a single briefing that pins down the Contentful-to-SFCC integration pattern, the content model SFCC must consume, locale setup, and the SFCC-side build scope, so the two teams share one boundary before the dedicated Contentful squad onboards.

- **In scope:** SFCC/MRT-side integration design, content-model requirements SFCC must consume, locale configuration, and the Accenture-vs-Contentful-squad handoff boundary.
- **Out of scope:** the full Contentful setup owned by the incoming squad (content authoring, Studio operations, the separate Contentful SOW). Linked, not specified here.

Contentful is the sole CMS across all Zimmermann storefronts (HPC-001): editorial modules, banners, size-guide fallback content, promotional content, and global assets. SFCC owns all commerce data; Contentful owns editorial. This spike is the same work item tracked as Open Item #3 ("Define Contentful content model and connector customisation scope") on [TSD: Product, SFCC Catalogue & Data Integration](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/292061208). Ticket: [SFCC-123](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-123).

## 1. Integration architecture & data flow [DoD-1 · Task-1]

**Target pattern** (per [`.docs/integration/02-contentful.md`](../integration/02-contentful.md) §3-§5 and [Technical Solution Design, PWA](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/256835585) §7): Contentful to MRT (Node/SSR) to browser, SSR-first for SEO and LCP.

```
PWA (SSR, then CSR hydration)
   ├──► Contentful Delivery API (CDA)      published content, SSR + browser; public token, safe in bundle
   ├──► Contentful Preview API (CPA)        drafts, MRT proxy only; token server-side, never in browser
   ├──► Contentful Images API               images.ctfassets.net, srcset/sizes, AVIF then WebP fallback
   ├──► GraphQL Content API                 composed pages, one request, field-projected
   └──◄  Publish webhook → MRT /webhooks/contentful   HMAC-verified; clears SSR cache keys
```

| Surface | Origin / boundary | Token | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| CDA (published) | Browser + SSR | `CONTENTFUL_DELIVERY_TOKEN` (public, read-only) | SSR-first target; held as an MRT env var so rotation is centralised |
| CPA (drafts) | MRT proxy only | `CONTENTFUL_PREVIEW_TOKEN` (server-side) | Studio live preview via iframe `postMessage` |
| CMA (schema sync) | CI / local only | `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN` | Never in MRT or the bundle; build-time only |
| Publish webhook | Contentful to MRT | `CMS_WEBHOOK_SECRET` (HMAC) | Cache purge; 60s SWR TTL fallback |

CDN limit: 55 uncached requests per second per CDA token, absorbed by the SSR cache. Single Contentful Space, one environment per delivery tier (see §4).

> **Current implementation vs target (verified in code).** The live data layer is [`overrides/app/hooks/useContentful.ts`](../../overrides/app/hooks/useContentful.ts): two hooks (`useContentfulEntry`, `useContentfulEntries`) that fetch **browser-side over REST** from `cdn.contentful.com` (CDA) or `preview.contentful.com` (CPA) with `include=2` to resolve linked assets. Config comes from [`overrides/app/config/contentful.ts`](../../overrides/app/config/contentful.ts) via `getContentfulConfig()` (which wraps the PWA Kit `ssr-config` `getConfig()`). The **SSR-first fetch, the GraphQL Content API, and the publish-webhook receiver are documented as the target but are not yet in the code** (see §3 and §6, items 3 and 10). This is deliberate build scope, not a defect, but the briefing should not imply SSR editorial is live today.

## 2. Content model requirements [DoD-2 · Task-2]

**What exists in code today (verified):**

- **Studio Experiences** (drag-and-drop, registered via `@contentful/experiences-sdk-react` in [`experiences/definitions.ts`](../../overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/definitions.ts), autogenerated from the `.tsx` sources): `collection-hero`, `image-text`, `shoppable-image`.
